plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3) × value. My value is $21, so optimal bid ≈ $14. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive against Betty and Charles' likely similarly-shaded bids.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which for n=3 bidders is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $22, so I'll bid approximately $14.7, which maximizes expected profit given the equilibrium strategy assuming other bidders behave similarly rationally.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, where n=3. This gives a bid of value*(2/3). My value is $13, so I'll bid approximately $8.7. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin if I win, following Bayesian-Nash equilibrium logic for symmetric uniform-value first-price auctions.
